result: Transitive linear reversibility of a finite-dimensional norm sphere forces an inner-product norm up to scale
assumptions: compact group of linear norm isometries
transitive action on the norm unit sphere
proof_method: Haar-average an arbitrary inner product over the compact isometry group; transitivity makes the invariant Euclidean radius constant on the norm sphere; homogeneity identifies the norms up to scale

stress_tests.outcome: only p=2 passes the two-point Euclidean-radius transitivity witness for every tested n>=2

novelty_note: underlying compact-group/Banach-space theorem is standard; only PDT placement and executable audit are new repository work
open_boundary: transitivity Euclideanizes geometry but does not select n=3 or force TPI for a proper transitive reversible subgroup
